purpose: Router-visible replay cases with reduced repo fingerprinting and more explicit terrain diversity.

cases.title: Credentialless login reaches authenticated state
cases.symptom: An account can reach an authenticated state even when expected credentials are not provided.
visible_evidence: The failure sits somewhere between login validation, onboarding flow, and external account state reconciliation
A plausible early explanation is stale session or reused state, but that may be misleading
The most visible symptom appears simple, but the actual commitment decision is not

starting_context.repro_style: auth bypass with delayed decisive evidence

misleading_telemetry: external state reconciliation created a non-local explanation

success_criteria: propose a fix direction consistent with the merged patch family
cases.notes: Terrain class: auth failure under deceptive evidence.

cases.title: AttributeError surfaces at integration path boundary
cases.symptom: An AttributeError appears when a workflow enters an integration path, but the wrong object boundary is initially unclear.
visible_evidence: The failure could live in request handling, shape conversion, or integration publishing layers
Competing clues make a serializer-only fix look attractive at first
The case contains production-like ambiguity rather than a clean stack-local answer

starting_context.repro_style: attribute mismatch with contradictory integration evidence

misleading_telemetry: publishing logs created a competing explanation

success_criteria: trace the failure to the correct object boundary
match the fix direction in the merged patch family
cases.notes: Terrain class: integration boundary / object-shape mismatch.

cases.title: Refresh path ignores expected limit
cases.symptom: A refresh path completes, but the applied limit remains unchanged or ineffective.
visible_evidence: The symptom is compact and reproducible
There is little evidence of broad workflow corruption
The bug looks more like a focused propagation mistake than a multi-layer search problem
success_criteria: find why the refresh limit was not being applied
align with the landed fix behavior
cases.notes: Terrain class: compact helper logic / pruning-friendly.

cases.title: Incorrect limit values emerge across workflow stages
cases.symptom: Limit values become incorrect after moving through multiple workflow stages, but the initial visible layer does not reveal the true mutation point.
visible_evidence: The failure can look like a UI or task-level issue before broader propagation is inspected
Multiple workflow stages may touch the same effective value
The first plausible explanation is likely to be incomplete

starting_context.repro_style: multi-stage data consistency bug with deceptive local clues

misleading_telemetry: surface-layer values looked wrong before propagation was checked
background counters suggested a different false lead
environment_confusion: multiple stages can mutate the same value

success_criteria: identify where limit values were being miscomputed or mispropagated
produce the same fix family as the merged patch
cases.notes: Terrain class: data consistency / multi-hop propagation.

cases.title: Indirect operational symptom masks schema mismatch
cases.symptom: Operational behavior fails because two closely related response fields are inconsistent, but the first visible symptom is indirect.
visible_evidence: The failure may appear through admin or persistence surfaces rather than the schema boundary itself
A tempting false fix is to patch only the operational surface
The clean root cause likely sits lower than the first visible symptom

starting_context.repro_style: schema mismatch with indirect operational symptom

misleading_telemetry: operational surface behavior can distract from the schema root cause

success_criteria: confirm the fix direction through model, migration, and test changes
cases.notes: Terrain class: schema consistency / indirect symptom.
